text:
Berkly Catton is in his second NHL season, and Thursday night in Seattle looked like the one where it clicks. The Kraken's 2024 eighth overall pick scored three times in a 5-1 win over Vancouver, and Seattle snapped a three-game losing run (0-3-0) in a game it controlled from the opening faceoff.

The first period was a flood. Seattle put 24 shots on Leevi Meriläinen, the most the Kraken have ever had in a period according to Alison Lukan, and won the period 2.74 to 0.59 in expected goals (the quality of the chances). Catton opened it with a power-play slap shot at 7:37, but Jake DeBrusk tipped in a Vancouver power-play goal four minutes later and Meriläinen kept it 1-1, including a stop on Bobby McMann's 22% look.

The second period broke it open. Matty Beniers finished a 68% chance at 8:00, the goal that swung the game most by our numbers (Seattle's win chance went from 52% to 72%), and 54 seconds later Catton scored on a shot rated 1%. Jordan Eberle tipped in a power-play goal midway through the third, and Catton completed the hat trick on a feed from Frederick Gaudreau with 43 seconds left. Beniers was the engine all night: seven shots, a goal and an assist, and Seattle had 3.11 expected goals to 0.54 when he was on the ice.

Philipp Grubauer did the quiet part, 22 saves on 23 shots and 1.86 goals better than expected. Meriläinen faced 42 shots and saved more than his chances deserved too; Vancouver just couldn't get him any help. Daniel Wagner of Pass it to Bulis noted the 43 shots on goal were one short of the most the Canucks have allowed all season.

For Vancouver, it ends a two-game winning streak that followed a seven-game slide, and in Manny Malhotra's first season behind the bench, the bigger story sits off the ice: Elias Pettersson's name keeps showing up in trade talk, with Elliotte Friedman's reporting among the headlines this week. Nights like this one don't make the rebuild conversation any quieter.
headline: Berkly Catton's hat trick ends Seattle's skid
